claim: Wolfsburg-Braunschweig is a direct ~17-minute train with departures every ~30 minutes.
quote: There is a direct train departing from Wolfsburg Hauptbahnhof and arriving at Braunschweig Hauptbahnhof, with services departing every 30 minutes every day, and the journey takes approximately 17 minutes.

claim: Braunschweig's top-ranked attractions are the Dom (Henry the Lion's burial place), the Happy Rizzi House and the Herzog Anton Ulrich Museum.
quote: Braunschweiger Dom - Rated 4.6/5 ... Happy Rizzi House - Rated 4.0/5 ... Herzog Anton Ulrich Museum - Rated 4.5/5 - One of Europe's oldest art museums

claim: Braunschweig is a medieval town often overlooked by tourists, making it a less-crowded easy half-day from Wolfsburg.
quote: Braunschweig (also known as Brunswick) is a quintessential German medieval town that basks in culture, pristine nature, outstanding architecture and glorious history.

claim: Wolfsburg to Hannover Hbf is ~35 min by direct ICE/IC every 30 min, ~83 km / ~56 min by car.
quote: 35 min is the average duration for direct trains... straight-line distance is 74 km, while the road distance is 83.6 km... Direct trains depart every 30 minutes... Driving: Takes approximately 56 minutes via the 83.6 km road route

claim: Celle's old town has 400+ half-timbered houses plus a Renaissance-Baroque ducal palace and is gateway to Lüneburg Heath.
quote: Celle boasts an enchanting Old Town with hundreds of timber-framed buildings and a palace uniting Renaissance and Baroque styles, situated on the banks of the River Aller with Lüneburg Heath on its doorstep.

claim: Magdeburg's Grüne Zitadelle is Hundertwasser's last completed work (2005), with guided tours at €12.50 lasting ~70 minutes.
quote: The building was completed in 2005 as Hundertwasser's last work... Tours last about 70 minutes and cost €12.50 for adults

claim: Wolfsburg to Magdeburg is ~66 km with direct ICE/IC trains as fast as 1h02 (avg 1h24), ~47 services per day.
quote: The fastest journey time takes 1 hour and 2 minutes, though it usually takes around 1 hour 24 minutes on average... distance from Wolfsburg Hbf to Magdeburg Hbf is around 41 miles (66 km)... around 47 trains per day

claim: Helmstedt-Marienborn was the largest and most important crossing on the former inner-German border; the Zonengrenz-Museum opened in 1992/94 covers escape, border construction and opening.
quote: Helmstedt-Marienborn was the largest and most important border crossing at the former inner-German border... open since 1992 and was officially opened on January 24, 1994.

claim: Hildesheim's Mariendom and Michaeliskirche have been UNESCO World Heritage since 1985, with famed Bernward bronze doors c.1020 and a painted wooden ceiling of 1300 parts.
quote: The Mariendom and Michaeliskirche have been UNESCO World Heritage sites since 1985... bronze doors and bronze column of Bernward from around 1020, and the wooden ceiling from around 1130, consisting of 1300 wooden parts

claim: Gifhorn's Internationales Mühlenmuseum is a 15-hectare open-air park with 13 mills from Greece, Spain, Portugal, France, Germany, Russia and Korea, ~3 hours to walk through.
quote: open-air museum in Gifhorn is home to 13 full-size mills from countries around the world, including mills from Greece, Spain, Portugal, France, Germany, Russia and Korea... 15-hectare exhibition grounds

claim: Lüneburg from Wolfsburg is ~94 km and takes ~1h33–2h11 by train (via Hannover), pushing it past the 1-hour threshold.
quote: Lüneburg and Wolfsburg are around 59 miles (94 km) apart... by train is expected to take around 2 hours 11 minutes, though it can take as little as 1 hour 33 minutes on the fastest services.

claim: Goslar's Altstadt, Kaiserpfalz and Rammelsberg mine collectively form the Harz UNESCO World Heritage site, with the Kaiserpfalz the largest Romanesque palace in Europe.
quote: Goslar boasts a UNESCO World Heritage status for having nearly 1,800 timber framed houses... Kaiserpfalz, built at the beginning of the 11th century, which is the largest Romanesque palace in Europe, and the Rammelsberg, one of the oldest mines in Germany

claim: The Happy Rizzi House (2001) was a collaboration between US pop artist James Rizzi and architect Konrad Kloster, sitting in Braunschweig's Magniviertel as an office block with cartoon facade.
quote: completed in 2001 through a collaboration between American pop artist James Rizzi and architect Konrad Kloster... facade is adorned with whimsical shapes, smiling faces, and vibrant hues
